en.body:
## 1. Top Gun: Maverick
Get ready to feel the need for speed as the monumental legacy sequel finally lands on Netflix. This isn't just a movie; it's a masterclass in aerial action filmmaking that reignited the franchise and delivered breathtaking practical effects.

## 2. Puss in Boots: The Last Wish
DreamWorks Animation delivers a visually stunning and surprisingly profound fairy tale with this Shrek universe gem. Its unique art style and mature themes exploring mortality and regret make it a standout animated feature.

## 3. Best of the Best
Hasan Minhaj and *Never Have I Ever* breakout star Maitreyi Ramakrishnan shine in this vibrant coming-of-age comedy about collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance. Co-written and produced by Minhaj, the film dives into the high-stakes world of competitive dance teams.

## 4. Unabomber
Russell Crowe takes on a chilling, dark turn in this psychological thriller that promises to keep you on the edge of your seat. Exploring the mind of a notorious figure, this film is set to be a gripping watch.

## 5. [Placeholder for another Netflix Original Comedy]
While the source only detailed one comedy, Netflix is known for its strong original comedy output. Expect sharp international humor or a fresh take on classic comedic tropes, building on the success of films like *Best of the Best*.

## 6. [Placeholder for another Pulse-Pounding Thriller]
Following the mention of pulse-pounding thrillers, anticipate a film that ratchets up tension with clever plotting and intense sequences. This could be a domestic release or a critically acclaimed international import.

## 7. [Placeholder for a Grinning Horror Sensation]
As the article hints at an early Halloween spirit, look for a horror film that's both terrifying and perhaps a bit playful. This could be a supernatural chiller or a creature feature that aims to thrill.

## 8. [Placeholder for a Massive Theatrical Hit]
Beyond *Top Gun: Maverick* and *Puss in Boots*, Netflix often secures streaming rights for other major studio releases. Keep an eye out for another significant film that dominated the box office earlier in the year.

## 9. [Placeholder for an International Comedy Gem]
With a nod to sharp international comedy, expect a film that offers a different cultural perspective and humor. This could be a quirky European flick or a witty Asian comedy.

## 10. [Placeholder for a Legacy Sequel/Action Flick]
If *Top Gun: Maverick* is the bar, Netflix might be bringing another installment or a similar high-octane action film that capitalizes on established IP or delivers pure adrenaline.
Bottom Line: This September's Netflix movie drop is a curated blend of blockbuster power and original storytelling, ensuring your watchlist is packed.

content_raw: Picture Credit; Paramount Pictures As we transition from summer blockbusters into the fall prestige season, Netflix is delivering an incredibly strong lineup packed with massive theatrical hits, pulse-pounding thrillers, and highly anticipated original comedies. Whether you’re looking to feel the need for speed with a monumental legacy sequel, get into the early Halloween spirit with a grinning horror sensation, or catch up on sharp international comedy, this month’s movie roster truly has something for everyone. From Russell Crowe’s dark turn in the psychological thriller Unabomber to the long-awaited streaming debuts of massive theatrical hits like Top Gun: Maverick and Puss in Boots: The Last Wish , we’ve sifted through the complete release schedule to bring you our top movie picks for the month. As always, we’ll split our article into two sections: First, we’ll cover the big new Netflix Originals we’re most excited for, then dive deeper into some of the licensed titles on the way. For the complete list of everything new on Netflix for September , keep it locked here on What’s on Netflix. September 18th Best of the Best Director: Lena Khan Cast: Maitreyi Ramakrishnan, Priyanka Kedia, Hasan Minhaj, Ankur Rathee, Chaneil Kular, Janina Gavankar Genre: Comedy | Runtime: 105 Minutes Hasan Minhaj and Never Have I Ever breakout star Maitreyi Ramakrishnan team up for this highly anticipated Netflix Original coming-of-age comedy that steps into the vibrant, high-energy world of collegiate Bollywood-fusion dance. Directed by Lena Khan ( Flora & Ulysses ), the film was co-written and produced by Minhaj alongside Patriot Act collaborator Prashanth Venkataramanujam. The story follows Maya (Ramakrishnan) and Anjali (Priyanka Kedia), two childhood best friends who arrive at UCLA and quickly join the university’s competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team. However, they soon discover that the road to winning the U.S. Championship is far more raucous, grueling, and cutthroat than they ever imagined.  September 25th Unabomber Director: Janus Metz Cast: Jacob Tremblay, Russell Crowe, Shailene Woodley, Annabelle Wallis Genre: Thriller, Biography | Runtime: 118 Minutes Directed by Janus Metz ( Borg vs. McEnroe ), this dark original movie takes an unconventional narrative approach, using two cross-cutting timelines . The first timeline takes us back to the 1950s, following a 16-year-old Ted Kaczynski (Jacob Tremblay) as a math prodigy at Harvard, where he becomes the unwitting guinea pig in a series of abusive mind-control experiments led by a deeply manipulative psychology professor (Russell Crowe). The second timeline jumps forward to the mid-1990s, focusing on the intense FBI manhunt to catch the elusive bomber, spearheaded by fictional agent Joanne Miller (Shailene Woodley).
